projects.title: Weather Service
projects.short: Parser strategies, configurable weather bots, and automated tests in one focused C# application.
projects.description: A console weather-processing application that accepts JSON or XML, creates bots from configuration, and sends parsed readings through an observer-based notification flow.
projects.overview: The interesting problem is how to change input formats and bot behavior without making the processing flow responsible for every detail. Separate parser strategies, bot factories, and a notifier give each concern a clear place in the design.
features: Interchangeable input parsing
JSON and XML parsers implement the same strategy interface and return a shared WeatherData model. A parser factory selects the implementation from the input format.
Configurable, independent bots
Rain, snow, and sun bots use enabled flags, threshold values, and response messages loaded from JSON configuration. Factory classes create their services.
Observer-based notification
A notifier registers bot services, avoids duplicate observer registrations, and distributes each parsed reading to its observers.
Tests and a CI definition

xUnit and FluentAssertions cover parser behavior, malformed inputs, parser selection, and bot construction. A GitHub Actions workflow defines restore, build, and test jobs on Linux, Windows, and macOS.
workflow: Configure the participants
Read bot configuration, construct bot services through factories, and register them with the notifier.
Choose and run a parser
Detect JSON or XML input, select its parser strategy, and deserialize it into the common weather model.
Evaluate bot responses
Notify the registered observers. Each bot evaluates its configured threshold before writing its response.
projects.skills: Strategy, Observer, Factory Method, interfaces, serialization, configuration, exception handling, parameterized tests, and GitHub Actions CI configuration.

proofs.label: One processing flow, interchangeable parsing
proofs.explanation: The provider calls the parser interface, then passes the resulting model to the notifier. Input parsing and bot behavior stay outside this method.

proofs.label: Notify through an interface
proofs.explanation: Each observer receives the same weather model through IWeatherBotService.

projects.title: Inventory Persistence
projects.short: An inventory service backed by interchangeable SQL Server and MongoDB repository implementations.
projects.description: A .NET inventory console application that connects the same product-management service to SQL Server through EF Core or MongoDB through its native driver.
projects.overview: This project explores a useful backend boundary: the inventory service uses a product repository contract, while separate adapters handle relational and document persistence. A factory selects the requested backend when the service is constructed.
features: A common storage contract
IProductRepository defines add, lookup, list, update, and delete operations. InventoryService delegates product operations through that interface.
Two concrete persistence adapters
The SQL Server repository uses an EF Core DbContext and SaveChanges. The MongoDB repository uses driver queries and document operations.
Factory-based backend selection
RepositoryFactory chooses a SQL Server or MongoDB implementation from DatabaseType. Each application instance uses its selected backend.
Product data and relational migrations
Products include name, price, currency, and quantity. The repository includes an EF Core migration and ordered product listing in both adapters.
workflow: Select a persistence backend
Pass the desired DatabaseType when constructing the inventory service.
Create the matching adapter
The factory builds the database context and returns the corresponding IProductRepository implementation.
Use the shared product operations
The inventory service calls the repository contract while the selected adapter executes the database operation.
projects.skills: Repository and Factory patterns, interface-based boundaries, EF Core migrations, SQL Server, MongoDB.Driver, LINQ, CRUD operations, and relational versus document persistence.

proofs.label: Select an adapter at construction
proofs.explanation: The factory returns the same interface for either database implementation. Each service instance uses its selected persistence backend.

projects.title: Airport Booking
projects.short: Flight search and booking workflows with CSV import, model validation, and reflection-based rule descriptions.
projects.description: A console application for passenger bookings and manager flight operations, with composable searches, class-based pricing, CSV flight import, and automated query and validation tests.
projects.overview: Beyond the console interface, the project separates presentation, booking services, queries, repositories, and validation. Its distinctive feature is the use of custom attributes and reflection to display flight-field types and validation constraints.
features: Passenger and manager workflows
Passengers can search flights, choose a travel class, create bookings, modify them, and cancel them. Manager functionality includes booking filters and flight import.
Composable LINQ filters
Optional query parameters cover passenger, flight, class, price, departure and destination, airports, and dates. Filters are composed before materializing the result.
CSV input and model rules
Imported flight rows are mapped into flight models and submitted to repository-level validation. Rules check prices, required location fields, and departure timing.
Self-describing validation metadata
FieldType and ValidationRule attributes describe model fields. Reflection reads those attributes to print rule details. xUnit and FluentAssertions tests cover flight validation and booking queries.
workflow: Load and validate flights
Read CSV rows, create flight objects, and submit them to the flight repository with model-level validation.
Search and make a booking
Apply the requested filters, select a flight and class, then validate and register the booking.
Manage an existing booking
Resolve the booking, check the passenger relationship, and apply a modification or cancellation through the booking service.
projects.skills: C# object-oriented design, service/query/repository separation, LINQ, custom attributes, reflection, CSV processing, domain validation, and xUnit parameterized tests.

proofs.label: Use metadata to explain the model
proofs.explanation: Reflection reads custom field attributes and turns them into validation-rule descriptions for the console interface.

projects.title: Library Database
projects.metric_label: From loan records to useful insights.
projects.short: A relational library schema with analytical SQL, stored procedures, functions, indexes, and status-change auditing.
projects.description: A SQL Server database project covering books, borrowers, and loans, with data constraints, reporting queries, stored procedures, scalar functions, index definitions, and an audit trigger.
projects.overview: This project shows the database work behind an application: modeling relationships, enforcing basic invariants, and answering operational questions in SQL. The reporting scripts cover borrowing frequency, active borrowers, popular genres, author popularity, and overdue analysis.
features: Relational integrity in the schema
Books and borrowers are related through loans. Primary and foreign keys, unique ISBN and email constraints, status checks, and loan-date checks encode rules in the database.
Analysis with CTEs and window functions
Reporting scripts use joins, grouped aggregates, CTEs, and DENSE_RANK to analyze borrowers, authors, genres, and loan activity.
Reusable database operations
Stored procedures cover borrower creation and borrowing reports. Scalar functions calculate borrowing frequency and overdue fees.
Index definitions and audit history
Five nonclustered index definitions target selected book and loan columns. An AFTER UPDATE trigger records book-status changes by comparing inserted and deleted rows.
workflow: Create and populate the model
Run the schema scripts and sample-data inserts for books, borrowers, and loans.
Query operational behavior
Use reporting scripts to inspect active loans, borrowing frequency, overdue records, and genre trends.
Encapsulate and audit operations
Call reusable procedures and functions, and capture book-status updates through the audit trigger.
projects.skills: Relational modeling, referential integrity, CHECK and UNIQUE constraints, T-SQL joins and aggregates, CTEs, window functions, stored procedures, scalar functions, triggers, and index design.

proofs.label: Rank borrowers from loan activity
proofs.code:
WITH BorrowedCounts AS (
    SELECT BorrowerID, COUNT(LoanID) AS BorrowCount
    FROM Loans
    GROUP BY BorrowerID
)
SELECT (Borrowers.FirstName +' '+ Borrowers.LastName) AS FullName , BorrowCount,
       DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY BorrowCount DESC) AS BorrowingRank
FROM Borrowers 
JOIN BorrowedCounts ON BorrowedCounts.BorrowerID = Borrowers.BorrowerID;
proofs.explanation: A CTE calculates borrowing counts; DENSE_RANK assigns equal rank to equal counts while preserving a compact ranking sequence.

projects.title: MedicoPortal
projects.short: A medical-records prototype connecting patient requests, doctor responses, profiles, and daily measurements.
projects.description: An academic team project with a React frontend and ASP.NET Core API for doctor discovery, patient requests, medical-record responses, and blood-pressure and blood-sugar measurements.
projects.overview: MedicoPortal connects several screens to a related data model and an API workflow. Patients browse doctors and submit requests; doctors respond with record entries; patients can review responses and their measurement history. The frontend and backend are maintained in separate public repositories.
features: Patient and doctor account flows
JWT-based sign-in and role-specific endpoints support patient and doctor registration, profile information, clinics, and medical specializations.
Requests connected to medical records
A patient submits a request to a doctor. A response can add allergy, medicine, chronic-disease, or general-report entries and mark the request as answered.
Measurement history and related data
Patients can add blood-pressure and blood-sugar records. EF Core models connect users, patients, doctors, clinics, requests, and the different record types.
Frontend-to-API integration
React forms submit requests with Axios and bearer tokens. The API provides answered-status filtering and pagination for patient and doctor request lists.
workflow: Find a doctor and submit a request
Browse doctors and their specializations, open a profile, and send a request through the React form.
Respond through the API
The doctor response endpoint creates the supplied medical-record entries and marks the corresponding request as answered.
Review records and measurements
The patient can inspect requests and responses and record daily blood-pressure or blood-sugar measurements.
projects.skills: ASP.NET Core REST endpoints, EF Core relationships, SQL Server, JWT claims, DTO mapping, filtered and paginated queries, React forms, Axios, and API integration in a team project.

proofs.label: Scope and filter a patient request list
proofs.explanation: The request query starts from the resolved patient and then applies the optional answered-status filter. The following source lines paginate the result.

projects.title: String Calculator Kata
projects.short: A compact calculator kata with parameterized tests for delimiters, invalid input, negative numbers, and numeric limits.
projects.description: A C# string-calculator exercise with custom delimiter handling, explicit errors, and xUnit tests using FluentAssertions and AutoFixture.
projects.overview: A small codebase makes behavior easy to examine. The calculator supports comma and newline separators, a custom delimiter prefix, and a numeric cutoff. The test class expresses expected results and error behavior as parameterized examples.
features: Defined parsing rules
Empty or whitespace input returns zero. The calculator supports comma/newline separators and a custom delimiter declared with a // prefix.
Explicit rejection behavior
Malformed numeric tokens raise FormatException. Negative numbers are collected and reported through NegativeNumbersNotAllowedException.
A clear numeric boundary
Parsed values greater than 1000 are excluded before summing; the tests include the input 1,1001 with an expected result of 1.
Parameterized examples

Three xUnit theory methods contain nine InlineData cases across valid results, malformed input, and negative-number errors. AutoFixture constructs the calculator and FluentAssertions expresses expectations.
workflow: Determine the separators
Use the custom delimiter declaration when present; otherwise accept commas and newline characters.
Parse and check the values
Convert tokens to integers, exclude values above 1000, and reject any remaining negative values.
Return or explain the result
Sum valid values or raise the corresponding parsing or negative-number exception.
projects.skills: Parameterized unit tests, boundary cases, exception assertions, xUnit theories, FluentAssertions, AutoFixture, LINQ, and focused method responsibilities.

proofs.label: Examples describe the expected behavior
proofs.explanation: The theory captures empty input, mixed separators, custom separators, and the value cutoff in a compact table of examples.
